name: Oyster Stew
author: Fannie Merritt Farmer (1896)
steps: Clean oysters by placing in a colander and pouring over them three-fourths cup cold water.
Carefully pick over oysters, reserve liquor, and heat it to boiling-point; strain through double cheese-cloth, add oysters, and cook until oysters are plump and edges begin to curl.
Remove oysters with skimmer, and put in tureen with butter, salt, and pepper.
Add oyster liquor strained a second time, and milk.

culture.text: From The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896) by Fannie Merritt Farmer. It popularized level, standardized measurements (cups and spoons) in American home kitchens, and stayed one of the best-selling cookbooks in the United States for decades.
